rv.q: I have seen regular productions of Peter Pan that treat the death of Tinker Bell more casually than it is handled here by writer, director and star Johnny McKnight. Yes, the fairy’s final moments are over-the-top – not a twitch of a limb unmilked – but it is with some sense of jeopardy that the audience is called upon to bring her back to life.
Johnny McKnight can put together and perform a terrific alternative panto.
This is a true festive treat from start to finish, full of Glaswegian humour and imbued with a message of inclusivity and kindness.

cn.t: Critics praise Johnny McKnight's irreverent panto as a hilariously daft, sparkly subversion of JM Barrie's classic, celebrating its cheeky humor, progressive heart, and willingness to chart its own wildly inventive course.
